newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ties with France remind German president of wife.
newsitem.headline: Ties with France remind German president of wife.

text.p: Franco-German relations remind German President Roman Herzog of his marriage.
On a state visit to Paris on Thursday, Herzog was asked at a news conference whether it was hard to set new directions in the intensive relationship between France and Germany.
"Something that is so well played-in and normal doesn't create sensations every other week. It's really like my 38-year- old marriage, which despite that remains a deeply happy marriage," he joked.

However he said European monetary union was an important new direction which France and Germany were resolved to take together, and added that there was room to boost cultural ties, citing plans for a Franco-German cultural summit next year.

Herzog said he hoped his four-day visit would stimulate debate among intellectuals in both countries on shared political and moral values, and make former East German human rights campaigners better known in France.

The president is accompanied by several of the activists who led the 1989 democracy movement against the former East German communist leadership, which led to the fall of the Berlin Wall and German unification.

Herzog, the first president of united Germany to visit France, inaugurated a conference on Thursday entitled "Bastille 1789/Berlin 1989" comparing the aspirations of the fathers of the French Revolution and of the East German democracy movement.
